# Visible Windows & Doors

> Family-owned window and door company based in San Diego, serving San Diego County and Southern California (including Los Angeles and Orange County). We sell, install, service, and repair windows and doors — including replacement windows, new-construction windows, entry and patio doors, sliding and folding systems, screens, glass, and hardware. Licensed contractor (CSL #1150682) with a 5.0-star Google rating.

## About

- **Business:** Visible Windows & Doors
- **Type:** Window & door sales, installation, service, and repair
- **Ownership:** Family-owned and hands-on — the team that helps select the product is the same team that installs and services it
- **Service area:** San Diego County (primary) — plus Los Angeles and Orange County, Southern California
- **License:** California CSL #1150682
- **Rating:** 5.0 stars on Google (all reviews 5-star)
- **Specialization:** European-style window and door systems; service and maintenance for existing Albertini windows and doors (Albertini is a service specialty, not a current sales product line)
- **Hours:** Monday–Saturday, 8:00 AM – 5:00 PM
- **Phone:** (858) 334-9071
- **Email:** contact@visiblewindowsanddoors.com

## Services

- **Sales:** Windows and doors for homeowners, remodelers, and contractors — replacement and new-construction windows, entry doors, patio doors, sliding and folding door systems.
- **Installation:** Replacement windows, new-construction windows, entry and patio doors, sliding and folding systems, lift-and-slide and multi-slide doors, bifold doors, and screens — including flashing and waterproofing.
- **Service & Repair:** Windows and doors that are hard to operate, damaged, misaligned, leaking, or not locking — rollers, tracks, handles, locks, glass, seals, and adjustments. Includes European tilt-and-turn hardware and existing Albertini systems.
- **Screens, Glass & Hardware:** Retractable and large-opening screens, screen repair, glass replacement, locks, handles, rollers, and tracks.

## Guides

- [Title 24 Window Requirements in 2026: What San Diego Homeowners Need to Know](https://www.visiblewindowsanddoors.com/resources/title-24-window-requirements-2026-san-diego): California's 2025 Energy Code applied to projects permitted from January 1, 2026. San Diego is Climate Zone 7 (coastal) or 10 (inland); the prescriptive maximum U-factor is 0.30 and maximum area-weighted SHGC is 0.23. The tighter 0.27 U-factor introduced in the 2025 code applies to Climate Zones 1–5, 11–14 and 16, and therefore does not apply to San Diego. Covers permits and the CF2R-ENV-01-E certificate of installation.
- [Sliding Glass Door Roller Replacement: When to Repair and When to Replace](https://www.visiblewindowsanddoors.com/resources/sliding-glass-door-roller-replacement-san-diego): Diagnosing a hard-to-open sliding door — worn rollers, damaged track, misalignment, or debris. Repair is usually correct when the frame and glass are sound; replacement when the frame is corroded or racked, the glass unit has failed, or parts are unavailable. Large-format, lift-and-slide and European systems require a specialist and manufacturer-matched parts.
- [Foggy Dual-Pane Windows: What Causes It, and Can It Be Fixed?](https://www.visiblewindowsanddoors.com/resources/foggy-dual-pane-windows-seal-failure): Condensation between the panes means the hermetic seal on the insulating glass unit has failed; the unit cannot be restored and must be replaced, though usually the glass unit only, not the whole window. Distinguishes the three kinds of condensation (between panes = failure; interior surface = indoor humidity; exterior surface = normal and a sign of good low-E performance). Explains why drill-and-vent 'defogging' is cosmetic rather than a repair. References IGMA TB 1205-89 and ASTM E2190.
- [Salt Air and Sand: Specifying Window and Door Hardware for Coastal San Diego](https://www.visiblewindowsanddoors.com/resources/coastal-salt-air-window-door-hardware-san-diego): Chlorides cause pitting corrosion and drive galvanic corrosion. Specify AAMA 2605 finishes near the coast (AAMA 2604 inland) and 316 marine-grade stainless rather than 304 for exposed hardware and fasteners. Note that AAMA 2605 replaced continuous ASTM B117 salt spray with the ASTM G85 Annex A5 cyclic test, so salt-spray hours are not comparable across specs. Includes a fresh-water rinse schedule by distance from the coast.
- [Resources index](https://www.visiblewindowsanddoors.com/resources): All window and door guides and technical references.
